div.head: V As 3[b]
div.ab: And ylce man ðe wille mot gebeten ylce gestale wiþ ðone teonde butan ylcum wite oþ gongdagas; ⁊ beo syþþan swa hit ær wæs.
[And ylce man ðe wille mot gebeten ylce gestale wiþ ðone teonde butan ylcum wite oþ gong-dagas; ⁊ beo syþþan swa hit ær wæs.]

(3, 1. Und jedermann, der will, darf jeden Diebstahl ohne jede Strafe, [nur] dem Kläger gegenüber büssen [von heute] bis zu den Processionstagen; weiterhin jedoch bleibe es [das Strafrecht], wie es zuvor gewesen ist. Ld)

(And everyone who wishes may compensate for any theft without any fine, [only] to the plaintiff, [from today] until the Rogation days; thereafter, however, let it [the penal law] remain as it was before. Ld)

And every man who so wishes may pay to his accuser compensation for every theft, without any manner of fine, until Rogation days. But after that it [the fine] shall be [paid], as it has been in the past.
And every man who wishes may compensate the accuser for every theft until Rogation days, without fine; after that it is to be as it was before.
div.note: Only in Ld; missing from H and Quadr. (so not in the archetype). In Ld, ‘Be werum’ (Schmid's App. VII, 2) follows.
This clause, hitherto known only from Lambard, is shown by Nowell's transcript to have been in Otho B. xi.

Der Satz fehlt H Q und stand also nicht in lq, geschweige im Archetyp. Er ist wahrscheinlich, wie sicher der Zusatz, den hier H anknüpft (IV As 6), Bruchstück eines Æthelstanschen Gesetzes. Die sprachliche Modernisierung und Verderbnis fallen wie in Ld’s früheren Kapiteln dem Schreiber und Drucker zur Last

The sentence is lacking in H Q and so did not stand in lq, let alone in the archetype. It is probably, as the addition that H attaches here (IV As 6) certainly is, a fragment of a law of Æthelstan. The linguistic modernisation and corruption are to be laid at the door of the scribe and the printer, as in Ld's earlier chapters
Also ohne Justizertrag für den Richter; s. Gl Amnestie 2. 3. Kurz darauf gewährte der König eine ähnliche Erlassung des Strafgeldes bis August: III As 3
Thus without judicial profit for the judge; see Gl Amnestie 2. 3. Shortly afterwards the king granted a similar remission of fines until August: III As 3

That is to say, that the suit might be settled privately out of court, and then no fine would be paid to the judge. Ine, cap. 52, expressly forbids such private settlements. ‘These secret compositions,’ says Thorpe (p. 134), ‘are forbidden by nearly every early code of Europe; for by such a proceeding both the judge and the crown lost their profits’ (cf. III As. cap. 3).
Cf. Alf. cap. 5 § 5; II As. cap. 13.
